analysis.title: Energy Transition Blog: Spain Proposes Renewables Mandates for Data Centers, New DOE Loan Supports Nuclear Deployments, and New Wind Capacity Deployments Rebound on Accelerated IRA Sunset
key_insights: Spain proposed legislation giving data center operators a five-year ramp to the 80% hourly renewable electricity requirement. Operators would start at 60%, rise to 70% in 2029, and reach 80% after five years. Previously 80% was required from the start.

Under the Spanish proposal, data centers would no longer need to secure offtake from new generation. Power could come from plants that started operating up to three years before data center energization.
Spain has about 1GW of installed data center capacity, expected to reach about 4GW by the end of the decade. About 75% of installed power capacity is renewable, mostly solar and wind.

The DOE announced a conditional loan of about $5B for Constellation (CEG, Not Rated) to accelerate nuclear project startups. It supports about 1.1GW of capacity in PJM, with reactors in Illinois, Maryland and Pennsylvania, and backs Constellation's long-term PPAs with nearly all major US hyperscalers.

Earlier in October the DOE gave a conditional loan of about $4B to Vistra (VST, Not Rated) for its nuclear buildout in PJM. BTIG expects continued federal support for nuclear projects, particularly in regions with higher grid stress.

Wood Mackenzie reported US wind turbine orders hit their highest level in about three years in 2Q26, with about 3GW ordered. Projects that began construction before July 4 have until 2030 to begin operations to qualify for tax credits under the OBBBA. Projects that did not must operate before the end of 2027.

BTIG says the wind order rush has largely de-risked the roughly 40GW of new onshore wind expected by 2030, as most projects are under construction. Offshore wind leases continue to face federal pushback.

Google (GOOGL, Not Rated) and Voltus (Private) expanded their virtual power plant agreement in PJM to about 1GW from about 100MW. The VPP supports 13 states, including Virginia, the largest data center hub.

Westinghouse (Private) plans to spend about $1B to add LEU+ fuel production capacity at its South Carolina plant by 2030. LEU+ is enriched to 5%-10% versus 3%-5% for conventional fuel and can enable uprates across the existing fleet. The plant will not come online in time for the DOE's UPRISE program deadline of 2029, which targets about 5GW of added capacity.
The DOE awarded about $900M to Orano Federal Services (Private) in 1Q26 to replace Russian imports with domestic LEU and LEU+ production.

Nano Nuclear Energy (NNE, Neutral) signed a nonbinding MoU with Hyundai Engineering (000720.KR, Not Rated) for EPC and related services on NNE's Illinois demonstrator. NNE expects first power in 2029-2030.

South Korea's NSSC is extending the operating licenses of two reactors by 10 years each. The reactors total about 1GW, began operating in 1984 and 1985, and have not operated since their licenses expired in 2024/25.

Innio (INIO, Not Rated) secured an order of about 620MW from a major hyperscaler for its gas engine power solution. The same customer bought about 1.1GW in July. BTIG says gas remains in high demand for data center loads because nuclear baseload is hard to source at commercial scale.

risk_factors: Offshore wind leases face continued pushback from the federal government.
Westinghouse's LEU+ plant will not come online in time for the 2029 UPRISE deadline.
SMR technology remains a 2030+ story, so near-term nuclear growth depends on restarting shuttered plants.
Projects that did not begin construction before July 4 must be operating before the end of 2027 to receive tax credits.
geopolitical: Spain proposed easing its data center renewable electricity requirement with a five-year ramp-up.
Federal government pushback on offshore wind leases.
DOE funding to replace Russian nuclear fuel imports with domestic LEU and LEU+ production (Orano award).
